subject: Mathematics
title: Jingling Coins
subtitle: Coins, notes and shopping
hero_picture: A colourful Kerala village festival ground with a giant wheel, bunting flags, an ice-cream booth and happy families; two children holding coins.

sections.heading: Coin exhibition
text: Anu and Jithu went to the village fest.
They saw many coins: 1, 2, 5, 10 and 20 rupees.
sections.caption: Coins at the exhibition
sections.picture: Children looking at a table displaying Indian coins of 1, 2, 5, 10 and 20 rupees in neat rows (no readable text).

sections.heading: Ice cream time
sections.caption: At the ice-cream booth
sections.picture: A girl and a boy at a colourful ice-cream booth, the girl handing over some paper notes to the seller.

sections.heading: Ride the giant wheel
sections.caption: Buying a ticket
sections.picture: Children at a small ticket counter near a giant wheel, one boy counting coins in his hand.

sections.heading: At the shop
text: A crayon box is 5 rupees. Watercolour is 10 rupees.
Add the prices to find the total.
sections.caption: Shopping for colours
sections.picture: A small stationery shop with crayons, watercolours and erasers on the shelves, a boy buying a box of crayons.

sections.heading: My piggy bank
text: The class opened its piggy bank.
They sorted the coins into sets of 10 rupees.
Count the sets to find how much money!
sections.caption: Counting the piggy bank
sections.picture: A clay piggy bank broken open on a table with coins spilling out; children sorting the coins into small heaps.

rhyme: Jingle, jingle, coins in my hand,
One, two, five, isn't it grand?
Buy an ice cream, cold and clean!
activity: Play shop with a friend. Use paper coins of 1, 2, 5 and 10 rupees to buy and sell.
talk: Name the coins you have seen.
What can you buy with 10 rupees?
summary: We use coins and notes to buy things; we add their values to pay the price.

questions.prompt: An ice cream costs 15 rupees. Which makes 15?
A crayon box is 5 rupees and watercolour is 10 rupees. Total?

questions.explanation: Notes are paper money; coins are metal.

questions.prompt: A ticket is 20 rupees. Jithu gives 10 + 10. Is it enough?
